newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-AUERBACH, HOLZMAN TO COACH ROOKIE GAME ON ALL-STAR WEEKEND.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-AUERBACH, HOLZMAN TO COACH ROOKIE GAME ON ALL-STAR WEEKEND.

text.p: Players from both sides will be seeing "Red" when Hall of Famers Red Auerbach and Red Holzman return to the sidelines for the first time in decades to serve as coaches for the NBA Rookie Game at All-Star Weekend.
The fourth annual Rookie Game, featuring 16 of the NBA's top first-year players, will be played Saturday, February 8, as part of NBA All-Star festivities in Cleveland.

Auerbach has served as coach, general manager or team president in the NBA since its inception in 1946-47, and Holzman, who has been involved with the NBA as a player or coach since 1948-49, were selected as part of the league's continuing celebration of its 50th anniversary.

Auerbach, whose name is synonymous with Boston Celtic basketball, has the second most coaching wins in NBA history with a 938-479 record and has been recognised by having the Coach of the Year trophy named in his honour.
In one of the most remarkable achievements in sports, Auerbach guided the Celtics to nine NBA championships, including eight in a row from 1958-59 through 1965-66.

Auerbach was elected to the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 1968. He removed himself from the bench for the 1966-67 season to concentrate on his duties as Celtics general manager and served in that capacity until 1984. He currently serves as team president.

Holzman, who compiled a record of 696-604, guided the New York Knicks to the 1970 and 1973 NBA championships. He was inducted into the Hall of fame in 1985 and currently serves as a consultant for the Knicks.
